title: End of the page: freeze the fading section's shimmer, or fade it out under a flat cover
problem:
You asked (T-204 #32) whether the fade of the last section costs frames.

At the end of the page the big end panel grows over the last section (the four feature rows: Document, Discovered, Payment, Relationship).
Over the first 55 % of that growth the section fades out: blurrier (up to 12 px) and more transparent, until it is invisible.

What the section does meanwhile (Chrome counts, OBSERVED):
- It keeps 40 drawing layers.
- 5 endless shimmers keep running: 3 colour sweeps over the row titles (4 s each) and 2 glints on the Payment picture (5 s).
- They keep running after the section is fully invisible.
- The blur covers the whole section, a full screen of picture, on every frame of the fade.

A third change needs no decision: pausing the shimmers once the section is fully invisible.
- It changes no pixel: 0 difference in Chrome.
- In Safari only the usual 45 px² of noise in the nav logo shows, the same as with no change.
- It goes into the next build by itself. This proposal is about the two changes you would see.
idea:
Two ways to make the fade cheaper; each has a Try-it on the phone.
- (a) Freeze the shimmers from the first moment of the fade. The blur and the fade stay as today.
- (b) Drop the blur and the section's transparency. A flat cover in the page colour (light grey, #f5f5f3) fades in over the section instead.
- With (b) the colours mix exactly as before, but nothing is blurred.
- With (b) the shimmers also freeze once the cover is fully opaque.

A in Try-it is today's best build (v9-final); B is v9-final plus the option.
risk:
Neither option has a phone timing number yet.
- The counts are from Chrome, which can't show the phone's graphics work (the GPU draws the blur and the layers).
- If you like one, the next step is a short phone check against v9-final.
- (b) changes touch phones only (the morph-scroll build); desktop keeps the blur fade.

options.name: freeze-while-fading
options.label: (a) Shimmers freeze as soon as the fade starts
options.idea:
The 3 title sweeps and 2 glints stop where they are when the fade starts.
- The blur and the fade stay exactly as today.
- Scroll back up and they continue from where they stopped.
options.looksSame:
The blur, the fade, the panel and every colour are unchanged.
- Only the shimmers stop moving while the section fades.
- Most of that time the section is already blurred and half transparent.
visualDiff:
Still frames: no difference, 0 px² at every position.
- Chrome at phone size (430x775), 18 positions through the end morph, compared like for like (your pixel rule, PR-010).
The change is in motion only: the colour sweeps and glints stop moving during the fade. A still-frame check can't see that, so please judge it in Try-it.

gain.what: Shimmers running while the section fades
gain.how: Chrome page probe at phone size (430x932), counts only, at 45 % of the fade. Not a timing test.

options.risk:
The frozen shimmer is a visible change, small and only during the fade.
- The gain is GPU and animation work Chrome can't time; the phone may show no difference.

shots.caption: Fade half done (430x775), still frame: identical. The change is motion only (shimmers stop).

options.name: flat-cover
options.label: (b) A flat cover fades in instead of the blur
options.idea:
The section stays sharp and still; a flat light-grey cover fades in over it.
- The colours mix as before, but the section is no longer blurred.
- Once the cover is fully opaque the shimmers stop (they can't be seen).
options.looksSame: The start (no fade) and the end (section gone) look the same as today. The panel, the nav and the page colours are unchanged.
visualDiff: Chrome at phone size (430x775), 18 positions through the end morph, compared like for like (your pixel rule, PR-010).

During the fade the section is sharp instead of blurred.
- 10 % of the screen differs at the first step, up to 26 % (88,237 px²) at 19 % of the morph, 4.5 % near the end of the fade.
Largest shade difference 205 of 255, at text and picture edges (sharp against blurred). Flat areas match: the colour mix is the same.
Before the fade and once the section is gone: 0 px² (the panel and the nav are unchanged).
This is far above your pixel rule's limit (PR-010: 0.5 % of the screen), so it is your call.

gain.what: Blur on the whole section, each fade frame
gain.how: Chrome computed style on the section at phone size (430x932). A full-screen blur is GPU work, which Chrome can't time here.

gain.what: Shimmers running once the section is gone

gain.how: Chrome layer tree: the cover is one extra layer.

options.risk:
The section fades out sharp instead of blurred.
- That is a visible change for about half a screen of scrolling.
- The saving is GPU work, so only a phone check can show whether it helps.

shots.caption: 19 % into the end morph (430x775): A blurred and faded, B sharp under the flat cover
Near the end of the fade (50 %): A almost gone, B almost covered; the difference is small here

recommended.why:
(b) is the only option that removes the full-screen blur.
- That blur is the largest graphics cost in the fade.
- (a) only freezes small shimmers, which the next build already stops once the section is invisible.
